titulo.alumno: «Condizionale passato»: talking about a possibility that did not happen

intro: The compound conditional (condizionale passato) is used to talk about plans that could not be carried out, missed appointments or past duties left undone.

frases.estudio: Ieri sera ti ho cercato a lungo al concerto!
frases.alumno: Yesterday evening I looked for you for a long time at the concert!

frases.estudio: Mi dispiace tanto! Sarei venuta volentieri, ma ho avuto un contrattempo.
frases.alumno: I'm so sorry! I would have come gladly, but I had a setback.

frases.estudio: Avrei voluto presentarti i miei colleghi di lavoro.
frases.alumno: I would have wanted to introduce you to my work colleagues.
analisis: I would have wanted to introduce you

frases.estudio: Ti avrei chiamato, ma la batteria del telefono era scarica.
frases.alumno: I would have called you, but my phone battery was flat.

texto: It is formed with the simple conditional of the auxiliary (**avrei** or **sarei**) plus the past participle of the main verb.

With verbs that take **essere** the agreement of gender and number applies: **Sarei venuta volentieri** (I would have come gladly, if you are a woman), **Saremmo partiti presto** (we would have left early). With **avere** the participle ends in **-o**: **Avrei voluto parlare con te**.

filas.texto: I would have gone gladly, but I couldn't.
Ti avrei presentato i miei colleghi.
I would have wanted to introduce them to you, but you didn't come.
Avrei telefonato, ma il telefono era scarico.
I couldn't call because my battery ran out.
You should have let me know in advance.

pregunta.texto: Why didn't Silvia attend the concert with Paolo?

opciones.texto: Because an unforeseen setback came up that prevented her from going.
opciones.explicacion: Silvia makes clear: «ho avuto un contrattempo», although she would have gone gladly.

opciones.texto: Because she completely forgot the day and time of the appointment.
opciones.explicacion: She remembered the concert perfectly well but ran into an insurmountable obstacle.

opciones.texto: Because she preferred to stay at home resting with her colleagues.
opciones.explicacion: She states firmly that she would have taken part willingly.

frase.texto: Silvia è una donna, quindi dice: «Io ___ venuta molto volentieri».

opciones.explicacion: With the auxiliary «essere» the participle agrees in the feminine singular: «sarei venuta».
«Venire» is an intransitive verb of movement that requires the auxiliary «essere».
It is the first person plural of the simple future.

pregunta.texto: Why did the phone call not take place?

frase.texto: Ti avrei chiamato subito per avvisarti.

opciones.texto: Because the battery of her mobile phone had completely run out.
opciones.explicacion: It explains the technical impossibility of warning in time.

opciones.texto: Because she did not remember her friend's phone number.
opciones.explicacion: She had the contact but the device had no charge.

opciones.texto: Because she decided not to let him know, to surprise him live.
opciones.explicacion: She wanted to let him know, but the setback prevented her.

frase.texto: Sarei venuta volentieri ma ho avuto un contrattempo

piezas.traduccion: I would have come gladly but I had a setback.
piezas.explicacion: Expression of a frustrated possibility in the compound conditional with the auxiliary essere.

pregunta.texto: What cordial reproach does the sentence «Avresti dovuto avvisarmi prima» contain?

opciones.texto: It points out that the other person had a moral duty to warn in advance.
opciones.explicacion: «Avresti dovuto» makes a retrospective reproach about a neglected duty.

opciones.texto: It warns that tomorrow there will be a compulsory work meeting.
opciones.explicacion: It refers to a fact already completed in the past, not the future.

opciones.texto: It thanks the person for sending an urgent message in time.
opciones.explicacion: It points out precisely the lack of timely notice.

frase.texto: Noi ___ voluto partecipare alla conferenza, ma non abbiamo trovato posto.

opciones.explicacion: First person plural of the conditional of «avere» before the modal participle «voluto».
It is the first person singular («I would have wanted»).
The verb «volere» before a transitive infinitive is conjugated regularly with «avere».

pregunta.texto: What tense is used and what does it denote?

frase.texto: Avrei voluto presentarti i miei colleghi.

opciones.texto: Compound conditional: it denotes a wish that did not come about in the past.
opciones.explicacion: It expresses the missed opportunity to make the introduction of the colleagues.

opciones.texto: Imperfect: it denotes a habit they repeated every Friday.
opciones.explicacion: It is not a repeated habit but a one-off missed occasion.

opciones.texto: Future perfect: it denotes an action that will happen before next month.
opciones.explicacion: It deals with a fact that is already behind us in time.
